walkthroughs.body_html:
Component 3: Coursework Portfolio — a core area of GCSE English Language.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Component 3: Coursework Portfolio brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Component 3: Coursework Portfolio.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is a speech act according to Searle/Austin?
options: Vygotsky was a behaviourist who emphasised reinforcement.
An utterance that performs an action — promising, ordering, apologising, declaring. Speech acts have locutionary (what's said), illocutionary (intended force) and perlocutionary (effect) dimensions.
A speech act is any time someone speaks.
A speech act is a performance or a play.
Alternating between languages or varieties within a conversation or even a single utterance — often patterned by context, topic, identity or audience. Code-switching is rule-governed, not random.
A speech act is a performance or a play.
Code-switching shows the speaker doesn't know either language properly.
Code-switching means using slang words in formal speech.
